transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brings you here today?

Well, what brings me in is... I guess it's that my body just feels completely out of my control lately. Like, a few weeks ago, I couldn't stop moving. I was pacing around my apartment literally all night, just writing down all these ideas for a supper club I want to start. I had this whole concept mapped out, you know? Like, a speakeasy vibe but with molecular gastronomy. I used to work at this place downtown that did foam on everything, and the chef was this guy from Chicago who swore by it, but honestly, I think foam is kind of overrated now. People want texture, you know? But anyway, I was up all night pacing and planning that. And now... now I'm just so slowed down. My sister was here yesterday, and she got so annoyed because she said it took me forever just to put my shoes on. Which reminds me, I need to buy new shoes for work. The non-slip ones I have are completely worn out on the heels, and if I slip carrying a tray, my manager will absolutely lose it. He's already on my case about my availability since I dropped out of my classes last semester...
Have you ever had a period of time when your mood was unusually high, elevated, or irritable — like you felt on top of the world or extremely restless — that lasted for several days or more?

Yeah, actually. Like, right after I got fired from my last serving job... which was completely ridiculous by the way. They said I was "too intense" for the morning shift. Who even goes out for breakfast on a Tuesday? It’s just old guys reading the newspaper and drinking decaf. And decaf is such a scam, honestly. The chemicals they use to strip the caffeine out are probably way worse for your heart than just drinking regular coffee. My uncle drank decaf for twenty years and still had a heart attack, so what's the point? 

But anyway, yeah, after I got fired, I didn't even care. I felt weirdly unstoppable. Just buzzing and totally excited about everything I was gonna do next. I had all these massive plans. But if anyone—like my sister or my roommate—questioned my plans or told me I needed to slow down, I would just completely blow up at them. I'd scream at them because it felt like they were actively trying to ruin my life and hold me back. Which is weird because my roommate is usually super chill. He plays bass in this indie band that practices in our living room. They’re actually trying to get a gig at that new venue on 4th street, but the acoustics there are completely terrible, they have these high tin ceilings... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, feeling high or irritable. Yeah, I felt amazing, but I'd snap if anyone got in my way.
Can you tell me more about that time when you felt buzzing and excited after getting fired—how long did that feeling last?

How long did it last? Man, I don't even really know. Time was just completely irrelevant to me right then. It's kind of like when you're working a double shift and you lose all sense of day and night. Have you ever worked in a restaurant? It's literally a time warp. Especially during brunch. Brunch is an absolute nightmare. Everybody wants bottomless mimosas, but the orange juice machine at that place was constantly breaking down. It was this massive, silver industrial thing, probably older than I am, and it made this horrible grinding noise every time you used it. 

My manager refused to replace it because he was ridiculously cheap. Like, he wouldn't even buy us decent pens to take orders with. I always had to bring my own Pilot G2s. The 0.7 millimeter ones, obviously, because the 0.5s are way too scratchy on receipt paper. I actually ordered a massive bulk pack of them on Amazon right around that time because I decided I was going to write a screenplay about the restaurant industry. It was gonna be like that show *The Bear*, but way more authentic to the front-of-house staff, you know? I had already cast the whole thing in my head, and I was going to send it to A24... 

Wait, sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, how long the buzzing feeling lasted. Yeah, I honestly couldn't give you an exact number of days or anything. I wasn't keeping track of the calendar at all, so I really have no idea.
Was there a time when you felt that way — buzzing and excited — for at least a full week or more without needing much sleep or slowing down?

Yeah, a full week? Honestly, it was probably longer than that. I just had this nonstop energy. Like, I literally couldn't even sit through a meal or watch a soccer game on TV without jumping up because I had to make calls or sketch out these new menus for that supper club I was talking about. Or I'd start completely reorganizing the kitchen. Speaking of the kitchen, my roommate bought this new air fryer, which is supposedly this miracle appliance, right? But honestly, I think it just dries everything out. I tried making sweet potato fries in it last week, and they came out tasting like literal cardboard. And you know how expensive sweet potatoes are right now? It's ridiculous. The grocery store down the street jacked up all their prices because they remodeled and put in that fancy organic section. Like, I don't need a perfectly curated display of kale, I just need affordable produce. The lighting in there is so weird, too—it makes all the fruit look almost neon. But anyway, yeah, I just couldn't sit still for a second. I was constantly moving, doing something, planning something... just totally wired for days on end.
Was there a time when you felt this way — buzzing, excited, and needing little sleep — for seven days in a row or more?

Seven days? Yeah, definitely. I mean, it was at least a week, probably more like two, where I was just totally on fire. I think I slept maybe two hours a night, if that. But I wasn't even tired! It was incredible. I'd wake up at like 3:00 AM and just start painting. I decided I was going to be an abstract expressionist. I bought all these massive canvases and oil paints—which, by the way, oil paints are so incredibly expensive. And they smell! The fumes are intense. I had to open all the windows in the apartment, and it was freezing because it was the middle of February. 

My roommate was so mad about the cold, but he was always complaining about something. Like, he'd complain if I left a single mug in the sink, but then he'd leave his bass guitar cables snaking all over the living room floor like booby traps. I tripped over one and almost broke my ankle right before I got fired from the restaurant. Which would have been a disaster because working on your feet with a bad ankle is literally torture. I had a coworker who dropped a keg on his foot once, and they still made him work the dinner rush. The restaurant industry is just brutal like that. They don't care about you at all, you're just a number to them. 

But yeah, anyway, the painting... I was just going non-stop. I didn't need sleep, I didn't even want to sleep. There was just too much to do, you know? Seven days in a row, easy.
After that time when you felt so excited and needed little sleep, did you experience a period of at least two weeks where you felt down, hopeless, or lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, after all that energy, it just... stopped. It's like someone pulled the plug. For weeks, man. The stuff that usually keeps me steady—cooking, taking food photos, music, pickup soccer, even the volunteering I do—it all just feels completely flat now. Like, I know in my head I used to care about all of that, but I just can't make myself actually feel it anymore. 

Especially the food photos. I used to spend hours getting the plating right, but honestly, Instagram's algorithm is totally ruined now anyway. They push all these reels and video content, and if you just want to post a really well-lit, beautifully composed photo of a risotto, nobody even sees it. It's all about who can make the most obnoxious 15-second video with trending audio. My buddy Josh is obsessed with it. He literally bought a ring light for his phone, and he doesn't even cook! He just reviews fast food. Like, wow, another video of a guy eating a spicy chicken sandwich in his front seat, groundbreaking stuff. And he eats in his car, which is so gross to me. The smell of fryer grease just bakes into the upholstery. I got my car detailed once, paid like two hundred bucks for it, and the guy used this cheap vanilla air freshener spray that gave me a massive headache. Vanilla is the absolute worst scent, it's just so fake... 

Wait, what were you asking me? Oh, right, feeling down. Yeah, I just... I don't care about anything right now.
